A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V2XPnP framework and dataset. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original perception and prediction experiments across four collaboration modes, including component ablations and additional task benchmarks in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional baseline, compression, and communication-noise results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the PointPillar backbone, temporal and spatial attention modules, map fusion, one-step feature sharing, output heads, losses, and staged training procedure.

E1.justification: The dataset, task families, and VC/IC/V2V/I2I collaboration modes remain unchanged. Figure 6 extends tested communication conditions beyond v1's 100-ms delay and 0.2-m/0.2-degree noise case to delays up to 500 ms and noise up to 1 m/1 degree.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated CoBEVFlow*, FFNet*, V2X-ViT*, and DiscoNet* baselines across all four collaboration modes. V2VNet* and F-Cooper* remain in the new Appendix Table S1. Figure 5 also replaces F-Cooper* with FFNet* in the qualitative comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 changes the stated training budget from 20 to 30 epochs per stage. Figure 6 adds compression settings and a joint delay/localization-noise sweep. Splits, metrics, spatial ranges, and temporal horizons remain unchanged; the budget revision does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds an empirical compression-versus-EPA analysis and substantially broadens robustness analysis through multiple methods and noise severities. The direct noisy one-step versus multi-step comparison from v1 Table 2 is removed. The clean communication-strategy comparison and component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Four added baselines and Figure 6 substantially expand reported results, while V2XPnP's original benchmark scores remain. For VC, its 71.6 AP/48.2 EPA now compares with V2X-ViT* at 69.6/44.7: highlighted margins become 2.0/3.5 points, previously 5.6/9.5 against F-Cooper*. Figure 5 changes qualitative results, and Table 2 loses its explicit noisy-result rows. The dataset comparison also changes RCooper's reported agent count from two to four.

T1.justification: The mathematical task definitions, attention operations, EPA formula, and appendix loss definitions remain unchanged. Moving map encoding inline and expressing the weighted loss sum in prose preserve their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The main framework, dataset, and performance contributions remain. The introduction qualifies the research gap by acknowledging prior short-term temporal fusion and emphasizing longer-term tasks. The abstract and contribution list now explicitly specify 11 fusion models.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds an explanation attributing robustness shared by V2XPnP and V2X-ViT* to spatial attention, with V2XPnP's additional advantage attributed to temporal attention. It also clarifies local temporal aggregation before sharing. Existing multi-task optimization limitations remain in the renumbered appendix.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies scenario composition and static-object annotation practices, and adds a future code/data release statement. Appendix A.1 removes the explicit 176 x 100 feature-map dimensions with 256 channels and some baseline implementation descriptions. The PDFs do not establish an actual release.

R1.justification: Related work substantially revises the novelty context through occupancy-flow approaches and explicit discussion of FFNet, CoBEVFlow, SCOPE, and UniV2X. It distinguishes prior short-term temporal processing from the targeted longer-term fusion problem, alongside numerous citation additions and removals.

P1.justification: Focused rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, related work, and experiment narrative. A new Appendix B shifts subsequent appendix labels, and the author line changes. The main section order and most technical exposition are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 6 and Table S1, redistributes baseline rows, shortens Table 2, moves Tables 2–3, and replaces comparator panels in Figure 5. The framework and dataset illustrations remain unchanged; other changes largely involve local reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in the central performance and communication-efficiency claims. Relevant temporal and Transformer competitors substantially strengthen the comparisons, while Figure 6 supplies compression sensitivity evidence and broader robustness testing. The stronger baselines also calibrate the reported advantage more convincingly. Removing the direct noisy communication-strategy comparison and some implementation detail weakens specific aspects, but the improved comparative evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
